record.title: Reuters reports Anthropic’s cloud marketplace revenue concentration and compute commitments
record.summary: Reuters reported from a confidential Anthropic IPO filing it reviewed that Amazon and Google cloud marketplaces routed about 47% of Anthropic’s 2025 sales, with approximately $351 million in distribution fees. Reuters also reported $54.6 billion in non-cancellable hosting and computing commitments at end-2025 and more than $417 billion in total long-term commitments by early 2026. The accessible source is a Reuters republication; the confidential filing, calculations and fulfillment of commitments were not independently verified.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Reuters reported, citing a copy of Anthropic’s confidential IPO filing that it reviewed, that Amazon and Google cloud marketplaces accounted for about 47% of Anthropic’s 2025 sales. The filing itself was not publicly available in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Reuters reported about $351 million in distribution fees on $2.16 billion of cloud marketplace sales, $54.6 billion in non-cancellable hosting and computing commitments at the end of 2025, and total long-term commitments above $417 billion by early 2026. These reported values and interpretations were not independently recalculated from the confidential filing.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The accessible report says Amazon declined to comment and Anthropic and Alphabet did not respond to Reuters. This review found no publicly inspectable underlying filing or company confirmation of the reported figures.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported confidential IPO filing is not publicly inspectable in the reviewed source set, preventing direct checking of definitions, figures and caveats.
Provider-specific obligations, delivered capacity, actual usage, prices and switching/cancellation terms are not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If accurate, cloud marketplaces routed nearly half of Anthropic’s 2025 sales through two providers that also supply compute and hold investments, while long-term obligations reportedly exceeded $417 billion by early 2026. This scale could shape frontier-lab unit economics, access to compute and bargaining power, although the confidential filing and reported calculations have not been independently inspected.
limitations: Reuters attributes the figures to a confidential filing it reviewed; this review could not inspect that filing.
Reported commitments are not equivalent to realized spending, delivered capacity, utilization or payments.
The report’s cloud marketplace revenue, distribution-fee analysis and accounting interpretation were not independently recalculated.
Amazon declined to comment; Anthropic and Alphabet did not respond, according to Reuters.
The review did not establish comparable provider shares, contract terms, cancellation rights or matched cost/performance.

technical.claimed_result: Reuters reported marketplace and commitment figures attributed to a confidential filing; no technical performance result is claimed.
technical.compute_or_cost: The report states sales, fees and commitments but does not establish delivered compute, utilization, unit cost or matched performance.
technical.demonstrated_result: The reviewed public artifact demonstrates that Reuters published the report and attributes figures to a confidential filing it saw; it does not independently demonstrate the underlying financial figures.
technical.implementation_status: Reported financial commitments and marketplace sales; contract fulfillment and capacity delivery were not verified.
technical.mechanism: Cloud marketplaces distribute Claude and collect customer bills, while Amazon and Google also provide computing capacity and are investors, according to Reuters’ account of the filing.
technical.novelty: The report quantifies the overlap of distribution, compute supply, investment and competition in one frontier-model company’s relationships.
technical.regime: Anthropic’s reported 2025 revenue and commitments disclosed in a confidential IPO filing Reuters says it reviewed.
technical.reproducibility: The report is accessible, but the underlying filing and calculations are unavailable for independent reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Reuters reports marketplace sales rose from 11% of revenue in 2023 to 32% in 2024 and nearly half in 2025; those comparisons also rely on the filing.

brief.title: Reuters reports Anthropic’s cloud marketplace revenue concentration and compute commitments
brief.why_it_matters: The reported figures describe a potentially important economic structure: major cloud providers are simultaneously distribution channels, compute suppliers, investors and AI competitors. If accurate, this concentration and the scale of forward commitments could affect Anthropic’s cash collection, margins, compute access and bargaining power. The evidence remains a media account of a confidential filing, not independently verified financial data.
